profile.headline: Software Engineer at DNV GL
profile.summary:
I'm a generalist and, over my career, have had the opportunity to play a role in various aspects of the software development process.

- High level system architecture design
- Database modeling
- UI/UX development
- REST API design
- DevOps 
- CI 
- Test automation

I've worked as both an individual contributor and manager.  

I'm experienced with Java, Python, JavaScript and C#.

Currently, I'm working on a couple of projects utilizing ReactJS and React Native.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Working on software pertaining to electric grid asset management.

positions.title: Founder
positions.description: Developed a machine-learning based mobile app for counting living and dead cells on a microscope slide. The mobile client was built with ReactJS and Phonegap. The cell counting service was hosted in AWS and built in Python using Django Rest Framework for the API and scikit-learn for object detection in images.

positions.title: Senior Software Engineer
positions.description:
Established continuous integration (CI) infrastructure and company-wide testing best practices by installing Jenkins and automating test suites for all layers of the stack: django/python, JS/angular, and protractor/selenium.

Built out the devops infrastructure using SaltStack and AWS. 

Full integrated Jenkins, SaltStack, GitHub and AWS such that a build could be deployed to multiple EC2 instances at the click of a button.

Coded-up platform features that touched all layers of the stack: front-end/UI, server-side models and database.

positions.title: Staff Software Engineer
positions.description:
Developed and maintained SMRTPortal, a webapp that allowed customers to manage their experiments and view results. The UI was built with JQuery and the service layer API was built with Java Rest Framework (Java6).

Also, developed and maintained a number of command line applications, the primary one being a "genome indexer". It accepted a genome in FASTA format (of any size) as an argument and produced a set meta-documents that described the genome: number and length of contigs, location of invalid regions, bad headers, etc.
